new.n: The old Klondyke copper mine shaft, about a mile east of Henderson (reopened 1926)
new.pl: About a mile east of Henderson, in Tyrone Township on the east side of the Minnesota River; the shaft is not placed.
new.st: In August 1926 the mayor of Henderson planned to reopen the shaft of the old Klondyke copper mine about a mile east of town, negotiating a lease and buying machinery; he recalled 'the unsuccessful attempt to mine copper here in paying quantities in the past 40 years', which puts the shaft at about 1886. No production was ever reported. Pin: East Henderson; the shaft is not placed.
new.t: Minnesota River valley bluffs east of Henderson; a capped shaft or spoil heap would show on lidar. Private farmland and bluff: ask first.
pinev: East Henderson point 44.53,-93.90, r1600; the shaft is not placed.

set.st: Legend (Des Moines Register 1927): a lone Indian fleeing pursuers in 1832 with a heavy two-lobed sack of plunder crossed a clearing on what became the Christopher Meyer farm; at a spring about half a mile on he was seen without the sack and was later shot. Meyer built his house between the clearing and the spring and dug for years; his daughter Dora (Mrs. Timmerman) and the school children hunted the hummocks. Pin is the Meyer farm on the 1886 atlas, not the spot itself. The 1927 feature placed the hilltop at Brookman's Bluff near New Albin.
set.pl: Christopher Meyer farm, NE¼ sec 10 T100N R5W, Union City Twp (1886 atlas), about 9 mi W of New Albin; the clearing and the spring half a mile on are not yet fixed; the 1927 feature names Brookman's Bluff
